en.greeting: Hi! Today you'll learn phrasal verbs, like get up, turn on and look for: small word pairs you use every day. Let's go one step at a time.

steps.title: What is a phrasal verb?
steps.text: Let's start with a new word: phrasal verb. You already know some!
steps.body: A **phrasal verb** is a **verb** (an action word: *get, look, turn, put*) + a **small word** (*up, on, off, out, back, for, down*). Together they have a **new meaning**, so **don't translate word by word**: *get* = mendapat, but **get up** = bangun dari tempat tidur. *look* = melihat, but **look for** = mencari. You already know **sit down**, **stand up** and **wake up**. Learn each one as a whole, like a new word.

steps.title: Your day
steps.text: Four phrasal verbs for your routine: wake up, get up, go out, come back.
steps.body: **wake up** = your eyes open; **get up** = you leave the bed. Indonesian *bangun* is both. **go out** = keluar rumah, pergi main; **come back** = kembali, pulang. With he / she the **-s goes on the verb**: she **gets up**, never `get ups`. Negative: I **don't get up** early.

examples.en: I wake up at 4:30, but I get up at five.
examples.id: Saya bangun jam setengah lima, tapi baru turun dari tempat tidur jam lima.

examples.en: Rina goes out with her friends on Saturdays.
examples.id: Rina pergi main dengan teman-temannya setiap Sabtu.

examples.en: My father comes back from the office at six.
examples.id: Ayah saya pulang dari kantor jam enam.

examples.en: I don't go out on weekdays.
examples.id: Saya tidak pergi main di hari kerja.

examples.en: What time do you get up?
examples.id: Kamu bangun jam berapa?

steps.title: Build the sentence
steps.text: Talk about someone's routine. Watch where the -s goes.

question.prompt: Arrange the words: Saudara laki-laki saya tidak pernah bangun pagi.
question.solution: My brother never gets up early.
question.explanation: **get up** = bangun dari tempat tidur. My brother = he, so the **-s goes on the verb**: **gets** up. *never* goes before the verb, as with every simple present verb.

steps.title: At home: on, off, for
steps.text: Now the phrasal verbs you use at home every day.
steps.body: **turn on / turn off** = menyalakan / mematikan (light, TV, AC, fan). **put on / take off** = memakai / melepas (clothes, shoes, helmet). **look for** = mencari. **pick up** = mengambil, menjemput. Indonesian trap: *buka / tutup lampu* is **not** `open the light`: open / close is for doors and windows. And *mencari* needs **for**: not `looking my keys`. **switch on / off** is the same as turn on / off (common in British English).

pairs.en: We take off our shoes at the door.
pairs.id: Kami melepas sepatu di depan pintu.

pairs.en: Budi is looking for his keys.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: It's very hot in the office. What do you say?

question.prompt: The room is very hot. Complete: Can you ___ the AC, please?
question.explanation: It's hot, so you want the AC to work: **turn on** = menyalakan. `open the AC` comes from Indonesian *buka*; open is for doors and windows. **turn off** = mematikan, the opposite.

steps.title: Where does the thing go?
steps.text: One more thing: where to put the thing, like the light or your shoes.
steps.body: With **turn on/off, put on, take off, pick up** the thing can go after the small word **or** in the middle: *turn on the light* = *turn the light on*. But **it / them** (words for a thing: *it* = itu, -nya; *them* = mereka, -nya) go **only in the middle**: turn **it** on, put **them** on, never `put on it`. **Exception: look for never splits**: look for **it**, never `look it for`. Just remember it.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Only one of these is correct. Which one?

question.explanation: With **them**, the small word goes after it: pick **them** up. `looking my keys` needs **for** (looking for my keys), and `Put on them` should be **Put them on**.

steps.title: Guess from the context
steps.text: Don't know a phrasal verb? Look at the words around it.
steps.body: Light, TV, AC → **on / off**. Clothes, shoes, helmet → **put on / take off**. *I can't find ...* → **look for**. One phrasal verb can have more than one meaning: look at **pick up** below. The context tells you which one.

examples.en: There's a pen on the floor. Can you pick it up?
examples.id: Ada pulpen di lantai. Bisa tolong ambil?

examples.en: The phone is ringing. Can you pick it up?
examples.id: Teleponnya berdering. Bisa kamu angkat?

examples.en: Bu Ani picks up her son from school at two.
examples.id: Bu Ani menjemput anaknya dari sekolah jam dua.

examples.en: It's raining. Put on your jacket!
examples.id: Hujan. Pakai jaketmu!

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Read what Sari says and use the context.

question.prompt: Sari says: 'Where's my phone? It's not in my bag!' What is she doing?
question.explanation: *Where's my phone?* means she can't find it, so she's **looking for** it (mencari). She can't turn it off or pick it up: she doesn't know where it is.

steps.title: Flashcards
steps.text: Let's review the phrasal verbs. Say the meaning, then flip the card.

steps.text: Here's everything on one page. Keep it for your daily routine.

id.greeting: Hai! Hari ini kamu akan belajar phrasal verb, seperti get up, turn on dan look for: pasangan kata kecil yang kamu pakai setiap hari. Yuk, pelan-pelan satu langkah demi satu langkah.

steps.title: Apa itu phrasal verb?
steps.text: Kita mulai dengan istilah baru: phrasal verb. Kamu sebenarnya sudah kenal beberapa!
steps.body: **Phrasal verb** adalah **kata kerja** (kata untuk kegiatan: *get, look, turn, put*) + **kata kecil** (*up, on, off, out, back, for, down*). Bersama-sama artinya **baru**, jadi **jangan diterjemahkan kata per kata**: *get* = mendapat, tapi **get up** = bangun dari tempat tidur. *look* = melihat, tapi **look for** = mencari. Kamu sudah kenal **sit down**, **stand up** dan **wake up**. Hafalkan masing-masing secara utuh, seperti kosakata baru.

steps.title: Harimu
steps.text: Empat phrasal verb untuk rutinitasmu: wake up, get up, go out, come back.
steps.body: **wake up** = matamu terbuka; **get up** = kamu meninggalkan kasur. Bahasa Indonesia hanya punya *bangun*. **go out** = keluar rumah, pergi main; **come back** = kembali, pulang. Dengan he / she, **-s ditaruh di kata kerjanya**: she **gets up**, jangan pernah `get ups`. Negatif: I **don't get up** early.

examples.en: I wake up at 4:30, but I get up at five.
examples.id: Saya bangun jam setengah lima, tapi baru turun dari tempat tidur jam lima.

examples.en: Rina goes out with her friends on Saturdays.
examples.id: Rina pergi main dengan teman-temannya setiap Sabtu.

examples.en: My father comes back from the office at six.
examples.id: Ayah saya pulang dari kantor jam enam.

examples.en: I don't go out on weekdays.
examples.id: Saya tidak pergi main di hari kerja.

examples.en: What time do you get up?
examples.id: Kamu bangun jam berapa?

steps.title: Susun kalimatnya
steps.text: Ceritakan rutinitas seseorang. Perhatikan letak -s.

question.prompt: Susun kata-katanya: Saudara laki-laki saya tidak pernah bangun pagi.
question.solution: My brother never gets up early.
question.explanation: **get up** = bangun dari tempat tidur. My brother = he, jadi **-s ditaruh di kata kerjanya**: **gets** up. *never* ditaruh sebelum kata kerja, seperti kata kerja simple present lainnya.

steps.title: Di rumah: on, off, for
steps.text: Sekarang phrasal verb yang kamu pakai di rumah setiap hari.
steps.body: **turn on / turn off** = menyalakan / mematikan (lampu, TV, AC, kipas). **put on / take off** = memakai / melepas (baju, sepatu, helm). **look for** = mencari. **pick up** = mengambil, menjemput. Jebakan: *buka / tutup lampu* **bukan** `open the light`: open / close untuk pintu dan jendela. Dan *mencari* perlu **for**: bukan `looking my keys`. **switch on / off** sama dengan turn on / off (umum di bahasa Inggris British).

pairs.en: We take off our shoes at the door.
pairs.id: Kami melepas sepatu di depan pintu.

pairs.en: Budi is looking for his keys.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Kantornya panas sekali. Apa yang kamu katakan?

question.prompt: Ruangannya panas sekali. Lengkapi: Can you ___ the AC, please?
question.explanation: Panas, jadi kamu mau AC-nya menyala: **turn on** = menyalakan. `open the AC` berasal dari kata *buka*; open untuk pintu dan jendela. **turn off** = mematikan, kebalikannya.

steps.title: Bendanya ditaruh di mana?
steps.text: Satu hal lagi: di mana menaruh bendanya, seperti lampu atau sepatumu.
steps.body: Dengan **turn on/off, put on, take off, pick up**, bendanya boleh di belakang kata kecil **atau** di tengah: *turn on the light* = *turn the light on*. Tapi **it / them** (kata pengganti benda: *it* = itu, -nya; *them* = mereka, -nya) **hanya di tengah**: turn **it** on, put **them** on, jangan `put on it`. **Pengecualian: look for tidak pernah dipisah**: look for **it**, jangan `look it for`. Hafalkan saja.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Hanya satu yang benar. Yang mana?

question.explanation: Dengan **them**, kata kecilnya ditaruh setelahnya: pick **them** up. `looking my keys` perlu **for** (looking for my keys), dan `Put on them` seharusnya **Put them on**.

steps.title: Tebak dari konteks
steps.text: Tidak tahu sebuah phrasal verb? Lihat kata-kata di sekitarnya.
steps.body: Lampu, TV, AC → **on / off**. Baju, sepatu, helm → **put on / take off**. *I can't find ...* (saya tidak bisa menemukan ...) → **look for**. Satu phrasal verb bisa punya lebih dari satu arti: lihat **pick up** di bawah. Konteksnya yang memberi tahu arti yang mana.

examples.en: There's a pen on the floor. Can you pick it up?
examples.id: Ada pulpen di lantai. Bisa tolong ambil?

examples.en: The phone is ringing. Can you pick it up?
examples.id: Teleponnya berdering. Bisa kamu angkat?

examples.en: Bu Ani picks up her son from school at two.
examples.id: Bu Ani menjemput anaknya dari sekolah jam dua.

examples.en: It's raining. Put on your jacket!
examples.id: Hujan. Pakai jaketmu!

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Baca kata-kata Sari dan pakai konteksnya.

question.prompt: Sari bilang: 'Where's my phone? It's not in my bag!' Apa yang sedang dia lakukan?
question.explanation: *Where's my phone?* artinya dia tidak bisa menemukannya, jadi dia sedang **looking for** HP-nya (mencari). Dia tidak bisa mematikan atau mengambilnya: dia tidak tahu HP-nya di mana.

steps.title: Kartu hafalan
steps.text: Yuk ulangi phrasal verb-nya. Sebutkan artinya, lalu balik kartunya.

steps.title: Ringkasan
steps.text: Ini semuanya dalam satu halaman. Simpan untuk rutinitas harianmu.
